title: Green Light Filtering Glasses During Traumatic Brain Injury Rehabilitation
official: Efficacy of Narrow-Band Green Light Filtering Glasses for Symptom Management and Rehabilitation Participation During Traumatic Brain Injury Rehabilitation: A Randomized Crossover Pilot Study
summary: The purpose of this pilot study is to evaluate whether narrow-band green light filtering glasses improve symptom management and participation in rehabilitation among individuals recovering from traumatic brain injury (TBI). Common post-traumatic symptoms such as photophobia, headaches, difficulty concentrating, anxiety, and sleep disturbances may interfere with engagement in rehabilitation therapies and limit recovery. This study will examine whether use of green light filtering eyewear reduces symptom burden and improves participation in physical, occupational, and speech therapy sessions. Findings will provide preliminary evidence regarding the feasibility and potential clinical utility of green light filtering eyewear as a non-pharmacologic intervention during rehabilitation.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 to 70 years
* Diagnosis of mild, moderate or severe TBI
* Reports at least one of: photophobia, headach, concentration difficulty, anxiety symptoms ·
* Able to provide informed consent or consent via legally authorized representative
* Sufficient cognitive ability to complete study measures

Exclusion Criteria:

* Severe visual impairment (low vision, not related to injury)
* Active ophthalmologic disease
* Severe aphasia preventing participation
* Severe cognitive impairment preventing study participation
* Current use of therapeutic light-filtering glasses
* Medical instability
* Severe behavioral agitation
